prompt: Which of the following statement(s) is/are true for packet-switched networks?

source: NPTEL assignment solution in uploaded archive
prompt: Which of the following can be done with the help of NMAP tool?

options.text: Determine the services running on any target system.
Determine the OS of the target systems.
Identify the vulnerabilities of the target system.

explanation: NMAP can perform all of the above operations (except option d). NMAP can perform password attack; however, it uses the default dictionary available in the system. The correct options are (a), (b), (c) and (d).

source: NPTEL assignment solution in uploaded archive
prompt: Which of the following options cannot be used for host discovery using NMAP?
explanation: For host discovery using NMAP various options can be used, the most common option is ping sweep. –PE is used for ICMP ECHO Sweep, -PP and –PM is used for ICMP NON-ECHO ping sweep scanning. There is no option as –PC. The correct option is (b).

source: NPTEL assignment solution in uploaded archive
prompt: NPTEL Online Certification Courses Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur In ICMP (ECHO) sweep scan, a scanner sends an ICMP type-8 packet and receives an ICMP type- 0 packet from target. What does it indicate?
explanation: If the sender receives ICMP type-0 packet, this indicates that the target is up. The correct option is (a).

source: NPTEL assignment solution in uploaded archive
prompt: Which of the following NMAP options can be used for TCP sweep scan?
explanation: TCP sweep is carried out using the –PS, –PU option in NMAP. It is also done by some default options such as –sT, -p, -Pn. The correct option is (d).

There is no option called show-reason. The correct option is (d).

prompt: Which of the following sweep scans are automatically done when we use –sn option.
explanation: All type of sweep options are used with –sn option except UDP sweep. The correct options are (a), (b) and (c).

source: NPTEL assignment solution in uploaded archive
prompt: Which of the following NMAP options treats all hosts as online (skip host discovery)?
explanation: -sP is used for only determining if the host is online; -PO is used for IP protocol ping; -sU is used for UDP scan; -Pn is used to skip host discovery and treats all host as online The correct option is (d).

source: NPTEL assignment solution in uploaded archive
prompt: Which of the following NMAP options is used for Service and Version detection?
explanation: For OS detection –O option is used, we can also use –A option which is known as aggressive scan which can be used for OS, version and vulnerability scanning, for services and version detection –sV option is used. The correct option is (e).

source: Quiz question shared in this chat (checked against Week 12 concepts)
prompt: In an ICMP Echo sweep, if the scanner receives an ICMP Type 0 packet in response to an ICMP Type 8 request, what does this indicate?

options.text: The target host does not support ICMP

explanation: ICMP Type 8 is Echo Request; Type 0 is Echo Reply. A reply indicates the host responded.

source: Quiz question shared in this chat (checked against Week 12 concepts)
prompt: Which NMAP options can perform a TCP-based host-discovery sweep?
explanation: -PS sends TCP SYN probes; -PA sends TCP ACK probes. -PE is ICMP Echo and -PU is UDP.

source: Quiz question shared in this chat (checked against Week 12 concepts)
prompt: Which statement best describes nmap -sn?

options.text: It performs host discovery without port scanning
It skips host discovery and scans all ports
It only performs UDP port scanning

explanation: -sn disables port scanning and performs host discovery. Probe types depend on scan context and privileges; it does not mean all ICMP, TCP and UDP sweeps are always automatically performed.

source: Quiz question shared in this chat (checked against Week 12 concepts)
prompt: Which NMAP option treats hosts as online and skips host discovery?
explanation: -Pn skips host discovery and treats each target as online for the requested scan.

source: Quiz question shared in this chat (checked against Week 12 concepts)
prompt: Consider: (i) -sn performs host discovery only without port scanning. (ii) -Pn skips host discovery and treats hosts as online. Which is correct?
explanation: Both statements describe the options. -Pn does not itself mean “scan every port”; it skips discovery and proceeds with whatever scan was requested.
